newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 22.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Council slaps ban on pit bulls: Pit bull terriers are to be barred from the Kapiti Coast from July, and dogs with pit bull blood that are already registered will have to be neutered and have a microchip inserted. Page 1.

Secrecy concerns Anderton: Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Wednesday defended the Cabinet's secretive preparations for the signing of an international agreement liberalising foreign investment rules. Page 2.

Cabinet should be smaller -- Peters: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters, whose NZ First party is due to have three more MPs appointed ministers in October 1998, said on Wednesday the Cabinet should be smaller. Page 2.

NZ First silent during super referendum debate: Legislation paving the way for September's referendum on compulsory superannuation passed another stage in Parliament on Wednesday night with only one government MP speaking in favour of the scheme. Page 2.
Fernz eyes overseas investments: Fernz Corporation is looking at overseas chemical companies as future investments after the $105 million sale of its New Zealand fertiliser businesses. Page 13.
Projeted tax take lowered by $566m: The government's expected company tax take for the current financial year has plunged $566 million to $3.9 billion. Page 13.

More WestpacTrust brances to close: Some communities, including Stokes Valley, would be losing their last bank after WestpacTrust axed a further 13 branches next month, finance sector union FinSec said on Wednesday. Page 13.

UtiliCorp deal subject to approval: THe involvement of United States-based UtiliCorp in a proposal to run Power New Zealand as a joint-venture may be the first test of the government's policy on foreign investment. Page 13.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Students facing chase for debts: Bankruptcy 'loophole': Insolvency laws may be amended to force students declared bankrupt to pay off their student loans.
Skellerup break-up studied by Maine: Maine Investments is considering splitting Skellerup Group's struggling retail operations from its other businesses.

Airport 'needs' $1b outlay: Auckland International Airport will need about $1 billion in capital expenditure over the next 15 or 20 years to cope with its expected growth, the chief executive, John Goulter, said on Wednesday.

NZ slips in competition stakes: New Zealand has slipped from third to fifth in global competitiveness according to the annual survey of the World Economic Forum, an international grouping of government, business and academic leaders.

Motor Trade Finances lifts profit 26pc: The securitisation of about $400 million of its loan portfolio enabled the country's largest vehicle financier, Motor Trade Finances Ltd, to increase tax-paid profit for the six months to March 31 by 26 percent to a record $18.7 million.
THE PRESS
Public backlash at payout to twins: The stowaway Ingham twins, too poor to pay $20,000 in unpaid fines a week ago, have pocketed an estimated $30,000 for their story. Page 1.

English signals only one heart surgery provider: Whoever runs a Christchurch heart unit will have to perform surgery for the rest of the South Island, Health Minister Bill English signalled on Wednesday in Parliament. Page 4.

De facto legislation planned: De facto couples and the distribution of their property after a split will be covered for the first time under legislation to be introduced to government this year. Page 5.
Lower tax take hits govt surplus: The government on Wednesday revised its budget operating surplus downward for the year to June 1997, mostly because of lower tax revenue. Page 28.

Exploration encourages Enerco: Oil exploration results in Hawkes Bay were "very encouraging", the chief executive of Enerco NZ, Kevin Johnson, said in Christchurch, where he briefed analysts. Page 28.
Cedenco falls short of own expectations: Cedenco Foods has failed to meet its forecast of an interim profit. A loss of $940,000 was reported for the half year ending March 31. Page 28.

FCL Forests exports returns below budget: Fletcher Challenge export returns are down on budget over the last six months as the company fine-tunes its new radiata pine processing plants in Taupo and Kawerau. Page 28.
